Q: java.lang.SecurityException: Unknown calling package name, com.google.android.gms.common.internal.zzs A:

As of August 2025, @munsif even if you get the correct version you will get class duplicate error when compiling.

This is the tried and proven fix:

Do not use this lib:

implementation 'com.google.android.gms:play-services:17.0.0'

This is the correct lib:

implementation("com.google.android.gms:play-services-maps:17.0.0")

Why you ask? This will not cause duplicate errors.

By this type check the latest version.

Q: Why is my JavaScript function not showing alert message? A:

Try this to confirm the file is loading:

alert("JS loaded");

Why use an alert? It's not 1998 anymore - we have network tools in the browser where people can check properly and diagnose a problem it failed to load.

Q: How to center a button inside custom dropdown div(Netflix-style footer clone) A:

When using position: absolute in a element, if it's width and/or height are not specified, the size of the element will be calculated based on the left/right/top/bottom properties.

Your dropdown is positioned absolutely regarding the .footer-control containing block (closest parent with position: relative applied). What is missing in your code is applying right: 0; in the .lang-dropdown class.

This will make the element the same size as it's relative containing block, which in case is the .footer-control.

I've tried to reproduce your code to test using right: 0.

Note that, this works because the .footer-controls has the same width of the .lang-btn. I'm assuming that what you actually want is the dropdown to be the same width as the .lang-btn. In this case, you can make the .lang-btn position-relative and place the .lang-dropdown inside the button, which will cause the .lang-btn element to be the closest parent with position: relative.

It's somewhat confusing but once you grasp the concept of positioning elements, it becomes much clearer :)

Q: Multiple SQL Joins error in W3Schools Tryit Editor A:

Refer to their documentation here - https://www.w3schools.com/sql/sql_join_inner.asp

Section - "JOIN Three Tables"

If I re-write your code like below then it works fine in W3School's try it editor.

SELECT c.CustomerName, p.ProductName
FROM ( ( ( Customers c inner join Orders o on c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID )
    inner JOIN OrderDetails od on od.OrderID = o.OrderID )
    inner JOIN Products p on p.ProductID = od.ProductID );

Q: Reindex data from Elastic server to Elastic serverless A:

According to the official Elasticsearch 9.0 Migration Guide, the recommended way to move data from a self-managed or hosted cluster to Serverless is using Logstash with the Elasticsearch input/output plugins.

Solution: Migration via Logstash

This "push-based" approach bypasses the remote reindex limitation.

1. Prerequisites:

  • API Keys: Generate API keys for both source and destination. In the Elastic console, ensure you select the "Logstash" format from the dropdown (this creates the required id:api_key string).

  • Mappings: Ensure your index templates and mappings are already created in the Serverless project before starting.

2. Logstash Pipeline (migration.conf):

Ruby

input {
  elasticsearch {
    hosts    => ["https://source-cluster:443"]
    api_key  => "YOUR_SOURCE_API_KEY"
    index    => "test"
    docinfo  => true  # Required to preserve document IDs and metadata
  }
}

output {
  elasticsearch {
    hosts    => ["https://your-serverless-url:443"]
    api_key  => "YOUR_SERVERLESS_API_KEY"
    # This dynamically routes data to the same index name as the source
    index    => "%{[@metadata][input][elasticsearch][_index]}"
  }
}

3. Run the migration:

Bash

bin/logstash -f migration.conf

Why this is the best approach:

  • Metadata Preservation: Using docinfo => true and the [@metadata] reference in the output ensures that your _id and _index remain consistent.

  • Scalability: You can use the slices parameter in the input plugin if you need to parallelize the reading of large indices.

  • Reliability: Unlike the Reindex API, Logstash provides detailed logging if a specific document fails to ingest (e.g., due to mapping conflicts).
